texts.Demo:FileManagerOverviewIntro: File storage, browsing, uploads, and organization. Integrate with forms and rich text editors for media insertion.
texts.Demo:FileManagerOverviewAssetManagerDesc: Full browser with folder tree, copy/paste, properties panel, and multiple view modes.
texts.Demo:FileManagerOverviewFileBrowserDesc: Browse and select files. Flat list with search, filter, and grid/list views.
texts.Demo:FileManagerOverviewUploadDesc: File and image uploaders with drag-and-drop, structure selector, and optional folder path.
texts.Demo:FileManagerOverviewRichTextEditorDe: Rich text editor with media insertion from the file library.
texts.Demo:FileManagerOverviewFileStructureDes: How upload types are configured and differentiated by structure key.
texts.Demo:AssetManagerIntro: The FileManager component is a full-featured asset browser for managing files and folders.
texts.Demo:AssetManagerComponentDescription: Customize layout, behavior, and view mode to fit your use case.
texts.Demo:AssetManagerLayoutParamsDesc: ShowFolderTree, ShowTenantTree, ShowPropertiesPanel — control sidebar and selection details.
texts.Demo:AssetManagerBehaviorParamsDesc: AllowCreateFolders, AllowDragDrop, AllowMultiSelect — enable or disable operations.
texts.Demo:AssetManagerViewParamsDesc: InitialViewMode: LargeIcons, SmallIcons, List, Tiles, Details — choose default display.
texts.Demo:AssetManagerOptionalParamsDesc: StructureKey — filter by file structure. RefreshTrigger — force refresh when incremented.
texts.Demo:AssetManagerEventsParamsDesc: OnFileOpen, OnSelectionChanged, OnEditImage — respond to user actions.
texts.Demo:FileStructureIntro: Learn how File Structures differentiate upload types and validation rules.
texts.Demo:FileStructureWhatIsDescription: A File Structure is a named configuration that defines validation and processing rules for uploads. Different scenarios (e.g., avatars vs. documents) need different allowed types, max sizes, and processing options. Structures enable consistent validation and let you reuse the same upload components with different rules.
texts.Demo:FileStructureWellKnownKeysDescripti: General (mixed content), ProfilePicture (avatars), PublicAttachment (public documents). Configure in SpFileManagerOptions or the admin File Structures page.
texts.Demo:FileStructureComponentsDescription: SpFileUploader, SpQuickImageUploader, SpFileBrowser, FileManager (toolbar filter), and SpFileSelector all accept StructureKey to target a specific structure.
texts.Demo:FileStructureUploaderWithSelectorDe: Users can choose the target structure from a dropdown. Each structure defines different allowed types and max size.
texts.Demo:FileStructureCompareStructuresDescr: Both SpFileUploader (multi-file) and SpQuickImageUploader (single image) use the same StructureKey. Configure different structures (e.g., ProfilePicture for avatars) to apply different validation rules.
texts.Demo:FileStructureAvailableStructuresDes: Structures configured in the current tenant. Admin can create or modify via File Structures page.
texts.Demo:FileUploadBasicDescription: Upload components for files and images. SpFileUploader supports drag-and-drop and large files via HTTP; SpQuickImageUploader is for single-image use cases.
texts.Demo:FileUploaderFullDescription: Full uploader with drag-and-drop zone, Browse Files, progress tracking, and storage quota. Uses HTTP upload for large files (avoids SignalR timeout).
texts.Demo:FileUploaderWithStructureSelectorDe: Same as above but with a dropdown to choose the target file structure and Folder Path input (ShowFolderPathField=true).
texts.Demo:FileUploaderWithFolderPathDescripti: Uploads go to a fixed path (/web/demo). Folder Path input is hidden. Missing folders are created automatically.
texts.Demo:QuickImageUploaderDescription: Simple single-image uploader with preview and remove. Ideal for avatars, product main images, or any one-image picker.
texts.Demo:QuickImageUploaderWithStructureSele: Same as above but with a dropdown to choose the target file structure and Folder Path input (ShowFolderPathField=true). Useful for general areas where the structure is not predetermined.
texts.Demo:QuickImageUploaderWithFolderPathDes: Uploads go to a fixed path (/web/avatars). Folder Path input is hidden. Missing folders are created automatically.
texts.Demo:FileGalleryBasicDescription: Gallery view with search, filter by type, grid/list toggle, pagination, and lightbox preview. Supports optional selection and view/edit/delete actions.
texts.Demo:FileSelectorBasicDescription: Modal dialog for browsing and selecting existing files. Supports single or multi-select. Call ShowAsync() to open.
texts.Demo:GalleryUploadHint: No files yet? Upload some first via
texts.Demo:FileBrowserBasicDescription: Flat file list with search, filter by type, sort, grid/list views, upload, and bulk delete. No folder tree—ideal for entity-scoped files (e.g., Product images) or simple file galleries.
texts.Demo:FileManagerFullDescription: Folder tree, properties panel, and large icons. Best for power users who need full control over navigation and selection.
texts.Demo:FileManagerNoTreeDescription: Hides the folder sidebar. More space for files. Use breadcrumbs to navigate. Useful when embedding in constrained layouts.
texts.Demo:FileManagerNoPropertiesDescription: Simpler layout with no selection details sidebar. Focus on browsing without metadata.
texts.Demo:FileManagerMinimalDescription: No tree, no properties panel. Just the file view and toolbar. Ideal for embedded pickers or simple browse-only use.
texts.Demo:FileManagerListViewDescription: Compact list layout. Displays files in a dense, scannable list. Good for browsing many items.
texts.Demo:FileManagerSmallIconsDescription: Dense grid with smaller thumbnails. Fits more items on screen.

texts.Structure:General:Description: Upload any common file type: images, videos, documents (PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, PowerPoint, etc.), and audio. Suitable for general-purpose file storage.
texts.RequiredHint: At least one file must be uploaded
texts.ProvidersTabIntro: The storage provider determines where uploaded files for this structure are physically stored. Choose Database to store blobs in SQL Server, File System for a local or network path, or MinIO for S3-compatible object storage. Configuration is validated when you save.
texts.StorageProviderHint: The backend service where files will be stored. Database uses SQL Server blob storage; File System uses a folder path; MinIO is S3-compatible (e.g. MinIO, AWS S3).
texts.DatabaseConnectionStringHint: Leave empty to use the application's default connection. If you need a separate database, enter a standard SQL Server connection string. The connection is validated when saving.
texts.MinioConnectionHint: Enter your MinIO or S3-compatible endpoint and credentials. The bucket must exist and the access key must have create/write permissions. Connectivity is validated when saving.
texts.S3ConnectionHint: S3-compatible storage (AWS S3, MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, etc.). Leave endpoint empty for AWS S3; set a custom endpoint for MinIO or other S3-compatible services.
texts.S3EndPointHint: Leave empty for AWS S3. For MinIO use e.g. http://localhost:9000; for DigitalOcean Spaces use your region endpoint.
texts.FileStorageSettingsHint: Default storage configuration for file structures. When a structure has no custom provider override, these settings are used.
